I have/had the same issue. Ubuntu 24, Wayland, etc. I spent a day or two troubleshooting an was able to get thing working, for now. Had to remove/upgrade the mesa drivers for my Radeon 7900xt and install the latest. I also updated to the latest ROCm as I am using that. It was a huge pain as there were several different version of Mesa spread around the system why I don't know but just upgrading in place did not work. I had to be thorough. Now GoDot doesn't lock up the whole system when running the game. I was even able to switch it back to forward+. There are some residual issue with Vulkan support, but Godot is working. 

Upgraded to Mesa: 25.2.5, ROCm: 7.02

Of note, if anyone cares, if appears AMD is dropping starting to support the official Mesa Vulkan driver and not their own, this may have contributed to the issue. https://www.amd.com/en/resources/support-articles/release-notes/RN-AMDGPU-UNIFIED-LINUX-25-10-4.html

Hello,
for people with this problem after a driver or system upgrade, you can rollback your driver (which worked for me)

# Steps:

Close Godot etc

open mirrorlist and add a link to a previous time (I choose 21/08)
You can choose another one by changing time in the url

```bash
sudo nano /etc/pacman.d/mirrorlist
```

And add at the top the line:
```Server = https://archive.archlinux.org/repos/2025/08/21/$repo/os/$arch```

Then save (ctrl + X, Y (yes), enter)

then do rollback for mesa and vulkan-radeon
```bash
sudo pacman -Sy
sudo pacman -S mesa vulkan-radeon
```
reboot the system to be sure

**If all goes well, don't forget to delete the old mirror link (otherwise, you'll be locked out on that date).**
You can comment out the line.

_And be careful if you're performing a full system update. You can always block Mesa and Vulkan-Radeon if you really need a full system update._
